instructions.question: Which budget category does `transaction` belong to?
instructions.context: A transaction from a Canadian household's bank or credit-card statement. Amounts are in CAD. `description` is the statement line as the bank wrote it.

Transfers.what: Money moved between the household's own accounts or to/from a person: INTERAC e-Transfers to or from individuals, transfers to savings or chequing, paying off a credit card from the bank account, ATM cash withdrawals
Transfers.not_for: Paying a business (pick that business's category); loan payments (Debt Payments); investment contributions (Savings & Investing)

Income.what: Money coming in: salary and payroll deposits, freelance payments, interest earned, dividends, cashback, refunds and reimbursements from merchants
Income.not_for: Moving the household's own money between accounts (Transfers)

Dining & Take-out.what: Food and drink prepared by someone else: restaurants, fast food, coffee shops, bars, food delivery apps

Groceries.what: Supermarkets, grocery stores and farmers markets: food bought to cook at home

Entertainment & Recreation.what: Fun and media: streaming services, video games, movies, concerts and sporting events, hobbies, app and software subscriptions
Entertainment & Recreation.not_for: Gym or fitness memberships (Personal Care); travel bookings (Travel & Vacation)

Shopping.what: Buying goods: online retail, department stores, clothing and shoes, electronics, toys, gifts and flowers
Shopping.not_for: Groceries; pharmacy and medical items (Healthcare); furniture for the home (Housing)

Transportation.what: Getting around: fuel, public transit, rideshare and taxis, parking and tolls, car rental, car repairs
Transportation.not_for: Flights and hotels (Travel & Vacation); auto insurance (Insurance)

Debt Payments.what: Paying down debt: credit card balance payments seen on the card itself, student loan and personal loan payments
Debt Payments.not_for: Moving money from a bank account to pay a credit card (Transfers > Credit-Card Payment)

Utilities.what: Household services billed monthly: mobile phone, internet, natural gas and heating, hydro and water

Personal Care.what: Looking after yourself: gym memberships, fitness classes, hair and barber, cosmetics and skincare, spa and massage

Savings & Investing.what: Putting money into investments: brokerage, TFSA or RRSP contributions, crypto purchases, investment interest and dividends kept in the account
Savings & Investing.not_for: Plain transfers to a savings account (Transfers > To Savings)

Miscellaneous Fees.what: Bank and ATM fees, service charges, donations and charity, lottery, postage, office supplies

Insurance.what: Insurance premiums: auto, home or tenant, life

Education & Self-Improvement.what: Learning: courses and certificates, tuition, books and e-books, online learning apps
Education & Self-Improvement.not_for: School supplies for children (Child & Dependent Care)

Healthcare.what: Medical: pharmacies, prescriptions, doctor and dentist visits, medical devices

Housing.what: The home: rent or mortgage, condo or HOA fees, home repairs and maintenance, essential furniture

Travel & Vacation.what: Trips: flights, hotels and other accommodation

Shipping.what: Paying a courier or shipping company to send packages

Child & Dependent Care.what: Costs for children or dependants: school supplies, daycare, child care
